```{r}
#| label: function
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| warning: false
sample_farthest_point <- function(nb,
                                  res,
                                  sampling_area,
                                  seed) {

  # 1. Validate inputs
  if (!inherits(sampling_area, "sf")) {
    stop("Sampling_area must be sf objects.")
  }

  # 2. Prepare a permanent empty raster template (created ONCE)
  bbox <- sf::st_bbox(sampling_area)

  rast_template <- terra::rast(
    xmin  = bbox["xmin"],
    xmax  = bbox["xmax"],
    ymin  = bbox["ymin"],
    ymax  = bbox["ymax"],
    resolution = res,
    crs = sf::st_crs(sampling_area)$wkt
  )

  terra::values(rast_template) <- 1

  # 3. Select the first point randomly
  set.seed(seed)

  pt <- st_sample(sampling_area, 1, type = "random")

  # 4. Iteratively select farthest points
  for (i in 1:(nb-1)) {

    # Compute distance raster FROM currently selected points
    dist_raster <- terra::distance(rast_template, terra::vect(pt))

    # Mask raster
    dist_raster_masked <- terra::mask(dist_raster, sampling_area)

    # Plot results
    # plot(dist_raster_masked)
    # plot(pt, add = T, col = "red", pch = 16)

    # Locate farthest cell location within raster
    max_cell <- which.max(values(dist_raster_masked))
    farthest_cell <- rast(dist_raster_masked)
    values(farthest_cell) <- NA
    values(farthest_cell)[max_cell] <- 1

    # Randomly sample one point inside this cell
    farthest_cell_poly <- terra::as.polygons(farthest_cell)
    farthest_cell_poly <- sf::st_as_sf(farthest_cell_poly)
    set.seed(seed)
    new_pt <- st_sample(farthest_cell_poly, 1, type = "random")

    # Plot results
    # plot(new_pt, add = T, col = "blue", pch = 16)

    pt <- c(pt, new_pt)

  }

  return(pt)
}

smape <- function(actual, predicted) {
  (predicted - actual) / ((abs(actual) + abs(predicted)) / 2)
}
```

# **1** Introduction {-#introduction}

This appendix describes how the parameters of the Generic Region Merging (GRM) algorithm of the Orfeo ToolBox were calibrated to produce operationally plausible forest stands. FRI polygons were used as the target: parameters were chosen so that automated polygons match FRI polygons in density, area and shape. Three criteria were used: the symmetric percentage error of polygon density, and the overlap between the area-weighted distributions of polygon area and of polygon shape index. The example below covers one FMU (RMF) and one combination of metrics ("SPL only"), but the same procedure applies to any study area and any combination of input layers.

# **2** Calibration areas {-#sampling-area}

Calibration was carried out in Romeo Malette Forest, a predominantly coniferous FMU of northeastern Ontario, using ten 5 × 5 km square areas (@fig-base-data-1).

```{r}
#| label: fig-base-data-1
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Romeo Malette Forest and the ten 5 × 5 km calibration areas."
st_read("D:/00_Ontario_eFRI/03_shp_data/RMF/PolygonForest.shp", quiet = T) -> polygon_forest
  
st_read("D:/00_Ontario_eFRI/03_shp_data/RMF/ctg.shp", quiet = T) %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(polygon_forest)) -> ctg

ctg %>%
  st_geometry() %>%
  st_buffer(10) %>%
  st_union() %>%
  st_buffer(-10) %>% 
  st_transform(4326) -> area_clean

sat <- get_tiles(x = st_bbox(area_clean %>% st_buffer(5000)),
                 provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
                 zoom = 11,
                 crop = TRUE)
  
st_read("D:/00_Ontario_eFRI/07_analysis/segmentation/grm_parametrization/base_data/sampling_square_RMF.shp",
        quiet = T) %>% 
  st_transform(4326) -> sampling_square
  
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = sat*1.5) +
  geom_sf(data = sampling_square, fill = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = area_clean, fill = NA, color = "#FEFE62", lwd = 1) +  
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_bw()
```

\newpage

# **3** Parameters tested {-#parameters}

Three GRM parameters were varied:

- **Threshold**, the maximum heterogeneity allowed when merging regions, which controls how fine or coarse the segmentation is. A small threshold gives many small regions and a large threshold gives fewer, larger regions. Values from 10 to 100 were tested, in steps of 10.
- **Spectral weight**, the importance given to the similarity of input values when deciding whether regions merge. With a high weight, boundaries closely follow the input layers; with a low weight, shape criteria dominate. Values from 0.1 to 1 were tested, in steps of 0.1.
- **Spatial weight**, the importance given to compact and smooth shapes. With a high weight, the algorithm favours compact, smooth regions even when their values are less similar; with a low weight, boundaries mostly follow the input values. Values from 0.1 to 1 were tested, in steps of 0.1.

In total, 1,000 parameter combinations were tested.

# **4** Segmentation inputs {-#segmentation-input}

The "SPL only" scenario was used in this example. Its three input metrics are shown in @fig-base-data-7 to @fig-base-data-9:

- **z_p95:** 95th percentile of return heights above 1.3 m (dominant canopy height);
- **z_above2:** proportion of first returns above 2 m (canopy cover);
- **z_skew:** skewness of return heights above 1.3 m (vertical distribution of vegetation).

\newpage

# **5** Calibration criteria {-#analysis}

Three criteria compared each segmentation with the FRI polygons of the same area.

1. **Symmetric percentage error of polygon density (SMAPE):**

$$
SMAPE = \frac{\text{Predicted} - \text{Actual}}{\dfrac{|\text{Actual}| + |\text{Predicted}|}{2}}
$$

where Predicted is the polygon density of the automated delineation and Actual is that of the FRI. As defined here, the error is signed: it is positive when the automated delineation has more polygons per km² than the FRI, and negative when it has fewer. For example, with the retained parameters, the FRI has a density of 13.96 polygons/km² (3,102 polygons) and the segmentation 13.58 polygons/km² (2,943 polygons), giving a SMAPE of −0.03.

2. **Overlap of polygon area distributions:** the overlap between the kernel density of polygon area of the automated delineation and that of the FRI, computed at the pixel level so that each polygon is weighted by its area.

3. **Overlap of polygon shape distributions:** the same overlap computed for the shape index,

$$
ShapeIndex = \frac{\text{Perimeter}}{\sqrt{\pi \times \text{Area}}}
$$

which equals 2 for a circle and increases as polygons become more elongated or irregular. The shape index was computed on smoothed polygons, to avoid overestimating perimeters along the pixel grid.

These criteria rest on the assumption that automated polygons with the same distribution of density, area and shape as FRI polygons are operationally plausible stands.

\newpage

# **6** Results {-#results}

Results are presented for Romeo Malette Forest with the "SPL only" scenario. Parameter combinations with a SMAPE outside −0.1 to 0.1, that is, a difference in polygon density of more than about 10%, were first excluded (@fig-1).

```{r}
#| label: fig-1
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of polygon density based on threshold, weight of spectral homogeneity and weight of spatial homogeneity and where SMAPE values outside the range of -0.1 to 0.1 were excluded."
# Parameters
dens_threshold <- 0.1
weight_area <- 1/2
weight_shape <- 1/2

# Read data
readRDS("D:/00_Ontario_eFRI/07_analysis/segmentation/grm_parametrization/results/results.rds") %>%
  rename(dens_smape = dens_sspe) %>% 
  mutate(area_score = overlap_area_raster,
         shape_score = overlap_shape_smoothed_raster) %>%
  mutate(final_score = (weight_area*(1-area_score)) + (weight_shape*(1-shape_score))) %>%
  mutate_at(c("thresh", "spec", "spat"), as.numeric) -> results

# Compute for a specific forest and model and produce figures
selected_forest <- param$forests
selected_model <- names(param$models)

results %>%
  filter(forest == selected_forest) %>%
  filter(model_name == selected_model) %>%
  filter(dens_smape >= -dens_threshold & dens_smape <= dens_threshold) %>%
  mutate(parameters = paste0("thresh", thresh, "_spec", spec*100, "_spat", spat*100)) -> results_temp

# Color scaling
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#332288", "#117733", "#882235"))
col_scaled <- pal(100)[cut(results_temp$dens_smape, breaks = 100)]

# Size scaling
cex_scaled <- scales::rescale(results_temp$dens_smape, to = c(0.5, 2))

# Plot
s3d <- scatterplot3d(
  x = results_temp$thresh,
  y = results_temp$spec,
  z = results_temp$spat,
  color = col_scaled,
  pch = 16,
  cex.symbols = cex_scaled,
  xlab = "Threshold",
  ylab = "Weight of spectral homogeneity",
  zlab = "Weight of spatial homogeneity"
)
```

\newpage

Among the remaining combinations, the retained parameters were those that maximized both the area overlap and the shape overlap, that is, those with the lowest final score:

$$
\text{Final score} = 1 - \frac{\text{overlap}_{\text{area}} + \text{overlap}_{\text{shape}}}{2}
$$

In @fig-2, red circles indicate the best parameter sets.

```{r}
#| label: fig-2
#| echo: false
#| results: hide
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Final score polygon density based on threshold, weight of spectral homogeneity and weight of spatial homogeneity and where SMAPE values outside the range of -0.1 to 0.1 were excluded."
results_temp %>%
  arrange(final_score) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  dplyr::select(forest, model_name, thresh, spec, spat, overlap_area_raster, overlap_shape_smoothed_raster, n_forest, n_segmentation, dens_smape, final_score) -> best_parameters_temp

local({

# Color scaling
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("#117733", "#882235"))
col_scaled <- pal(100)[cut(results_temp$final_score, breaks = 100)]

# Size scaling
cex_scaled <- scales::rescale(results_temp$final_score, to = c(2, 0.5))

# Plot
s3d <- scatterplot3d(
  x = results_temp$thresh,
  y = results_temp$spec,
  z = results_temp$spat,
  color = col_scaled,
  pch = 16,
  cex.symbols = cex_scaled,
  xlab = "Threshold",
  ylab = "Weight of spectral homogeneity",
  zlab = "Weight of spatial homogeneity"
)

i <- which.min(results_temp$final_score)

coords <- s3d$xyz.convert(
  results_temp$thresh[i],
  results_temp$spec[i],
  results_temp$spat[i]
)

points(coords$x, coords$y, col = "red", pch = 19, cex = 2)

})
```

```{r}
  terra::rasterize(metrics, field = "shape_index") %>%
  terra::values(na.rm = TRUE) -> segmentation_smoothed_shape_index_raster

segmentation_smoothed_shape_index_raster[is.finite(segmentation_smoothed_shape_index_raster)] -> segmentation_smoothed_shape_index_raster

# Shape index in data frame
bind_rows(tibble(value = polygon_forest_shape_index_raster, type = "fri"),
          tibble(value = segmentation_shape_index_raster, type = "grm"),
          tibble(value = segmentation_smoothed_shape_index_raster, type = "grm_smoothed")) -> shape_index_data_frame
```

```{r}
  labs(x = "Polygon area (ha)",

        legend.title = element_blank())
```
